topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer opens the session by relating the material to prior practicals and outlining the day's learning objectives.

topics.label: Tumor virology, oncogene discovery, and transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the historical study of transforming viruses revealed cellular proto-oncogenes and established laboratory assays to assess cell transformation.

topics.label: Classification and functional mechanisms of cancer gene mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how oncogenic and tumor suppressor mutations are defined and illustrate their molecular mechanisms in cell cycle checkpoints and dominant negative effects.

topics.label: Mechanisms and consequences of sequence and chromosomal instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how specific defects in DNA repair pathways, replication machinery, and mitotic segregation generate sequence and chromosomal instability in cancer cells.

topics.label: Multistep tumorigenesis, hereditary predispositions, and tumor evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore models of sequential mutation accumulation in cancer development, inherited cancer syndromes, and the role of genomic alterations during disease progression.

topics.label: Lecture wrap-up and reading recommendations
topics.groupedBecause: The lecture concludes with administrative closing remarks, book recommendations, and a preview of the next lecture topic.
